newsitem.title: DUBAI: Yemen and partners closer to $5bln gas project.
newsitem.headline: Yemen and partners closer to $5bln gas project.

text.p: Yemen has made progress in talks with France's Total SA, U.S. Exxon Corp and Hunt Oil on firming equity shares in a consortium to develop a $5 billion liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Yemen, the London-based Arabic newspaper Al-Hayat reported on Thursday.
"Agreement was reached on most points under discussion, especially the basics of joining the project," the paper quoted Yemeni deputy Oil Minister Moheiddine al-Dhabi as saying.
"This asserts that the joining of Hunt and Exxon in the gas project has become imminent," al-Dhabi said.
The minister's comments came after talks in Paris between Yemeni officials and the firms from October 26 to November 1.
In January this year, Exxon, Hunt and South Korea's Yukong signed a memorandum of participation in the planned LNG project which will be operated by Total.
Under this agreement Hunt-Exxon would jointly hold 38 percent of the project's shares, Total 36 percent and the government 26 percent.
The proposed LNG plant at Balhaf on the Arabian Sea aims to export an annual five million tonnes of gas to Asian and European markets from the year 2001.
Neighbouring Abu Dhabi is already an LNG exporter and will be joined by Qatar by the end of this year and Oman by the turn of the decade.
